action: Deutsche Bank customers: expect notice from the bank and treat unexpected messages that cite the leak with caution. Compliance teams at banks: review what internal documents and personal data staff can export.
date_note: Date the media consortium published; how and when the files left the bank is not stated in the sources read.
exec: A leak of more than 15 million internal bank documents draws a data-protection inquiry in Hesse and shows the cost of weak control over internal data.
plain: More than 15 million internal Deutsche Bank documents have leaked and been reported on by news outlets. The bank's chief says account numbers, balances and logins were not affected.

key_findings: International media evaluated more than 15 million internal Deutsche Bank documents; a consortium including the Financial Times, Spiegel, the New York Times and ZDF reported on them.
CEO Christian Sewing said customer data such as account numbers, balances or login data are, in the bank's findings, not affected, and that the bank apologised to affected customers.

Hesse's data protection commissioner Alexander Rossnagel is checking whether the bank told affected customers without delay and has opened a general inquiry into possible GDPR breaches; the bank notified his office officially of the data outflow.

summary: Deutsche Bank is dealing with a data leak: media outlets evaluated more than 15 million internal documents. CEO Christian Sewing says customer data such as account numbers, balances and logins are not affected, per the bank's findings. Hesse's data protection commissioner is checking whether the bank informed affected customers in time and has opened a GDPR inquiry.
title: Deutsche Bank CEO concedes mistakes after leak; media evaluated 15 million internal documents, Hesse regulator investigates
